notes: CANONICAL FILE written by this event's own never-assessed initial research on 2026-09-08, standing in for proposals/treasury-buyback-cash-mgmt-2026-09-09.from-treasury-20y-bond-2026-09-15.json (the only proposal for this id), which is now shadowed and stays where it is. WHAT THE RESEARCH CHANGED FROM THE PROPOSAL, both stated because a canonical file should not silently inherit a claim it disproved. (1) IMPACT RAISED low -> medium. Every other buyback operation this calendar tracks is medium (treasury-buyback-10y20y-*, treasury-buyback-20y30y-*, treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06, treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09), and this one is 6.25x the size of any of them; filing the biggest operation on the schedule below the $2B ones was the inconsistency, not the tier. (2) THE PROPOSAL'S SIZE CLAIM IS OVERSTATED AND IS CORRECTED HERE. It reads 'larger than every long-end operation on the whole August-refunding schedule combined'; re-reading the same PDF row by row, the schedule carries nine long-end nominal operations (five 10Y-20Y, four 20Y-30Y) at $2B each = $18B, against this operation's $12.5B. The defensible version: $12.5B is 6.25x ANY SINGLE long-end operation (3.1x after sb0607's doubling), and the two September cash-management operations together ($25B) do exceed the long end's $18B — but one operation alone does not. WHAT SURVIVED AND IS NOW MEASURED: cash-management buybacks are a SEPARATE PROGRAMME from liquidity support, not a big version of one. All 26 on record (api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov buybacks_operations, 219 rows, fetched 2026-09-08) are 1Mo-2Y; they run in clusters around quarter-turns; they take the full cap 22 of 26 times and >=96% of it 24 of 26; and offers have exceeded the cap in every single one (min cover 1.43x), so a short fill is Treasury refusing prices, never running out of paper. TWO CAUTIONS INHERITED FROM THE PROPOSAL, both still true. The sector is 1Mo-2Y: it buys nothing at any tenor the long-end ledgers care about, so this is a cash/front-end supply signal, not duration support. And $12.5B is a ceiling, not a forecast. symbols: [], no house playbook is macro-keyed, and nothing here licenses an entry. CLOSE-OUT 2026-09-10 (docs/research/events/treasury-buyback-cash-mgmt-2026-09-09.md -> ## Outcome): the operation cleared its FULL $12.5B cap on $28.027B offered (2.242x), 27 issues, prices 93.832-100.258, and all three registered forward tests confirmed. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE CLAIMS ABOVE, recorded rather than smoothed because this file is the calendar's memory. (1) THE SIZE-RATIO FRAMING IS RETIRED. Treasury replaced the tentative schedule on 2026-09-09 (PDF re-fetched HTTP 200, 89,250 bytes, md5 c49a5351bf2d31a367817abc62be51bd, masthead 'For Publication September 9, 2026'), and sb0607's long-end increases printed larger than this file assumed: the 9/10 10Y-20Y operation went $2B -> $6 billion and six later long-end rows read '= or > $4 billion'. So $12.5B is 2.08x the next long-end operation, not 6.25x or 3.1x, and the two September cash-management operations ($25B) no longer exceed the long-end nominal total (now >=$34B, was $18B). (2) THE STRUCTURAL FINDING IS UNTOUCHED AND NOW STRONGER. The replacement schedule left both cash-management rows verbatim unchanged and added no third September operation, so sb0607 genuinely does not touch this programme's cap, sector or cadence. Base rates restated with 09-09 in them, re-pulled this session: n=27, all 1Mo-2Y, full cap 23 of 27, >=96% in 25 of 27, mean 95.5%, min 34.6%; offers exceeded the cap in 27 of 27. THE FINDING THE CLOSE-OUT ADDS: 09-09's eligible list was IDENTICAL to 09-03's (45 of 45 CUSIPs) yet offers fell only 0.87% ($28.272B -> $28.027B) after $12.5B had been retired from those same names six days earlier -- a fixed pool would have dropped ~44%. The offer book is a price-elastic flow, not a drainable stock, so a short fill in this programme is always Treasury refusing a price.
